I've pulled up your account, John. Let me share what I found so far:

**Account & line status for 555-123-2002:**
- Account status: **Active**
- Line status: **Active** (not suspended)
- Contract end date: 12/31/2026 — still valid
- Data usage: **8.7 GB of 15 GB** (Premium Plan) — well under your limit, so this isn't a data cutoff
- Billing: Your most recent issued bill (B1002, $150.00) is **not** in overdue status, so billing isn't causing a service block

So nothing on our end is restricting your line. That means the issue is most likely on the device side. Let's work through some diagnostics.

**Step 1 — Check your status bar.** Can you look at the top of your screen and tell me what icons you see? Specifically, I'm looking for:
- An airplane icon (✈️)
- Signal bars (or "No Signal")
- The network type (5G, 4G/LTE, etc.)

If you see an airplane icon, Airplane Mode is on and that would explain the complete loss of service.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check the status bar for you.

turns.thought:
Yes, exactly — that's almost certainly your culprit! Airplane Mode disables all of your phone's wireless radios (cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth), which is why you're seeing "No Service." The good news is that your line itself is in perfectly good standing, so once Airplane Mode is off, service should come right back.

**Here's how to turn it off:**

**On iPhone:**
1. Open **Settings**
2. At the very top of the list, you'll see **Airplane Mode** with the toggle switched to green/on
3. Tap the toggle to switch it **off** (it should turn gray)
   - *Shortcut:* Swipe down from the top-right corner to open Control Center, then tap the airplane icon so it's no longer highlighted orange

**On Android:**
1. Swipe down from the top of the screen **twice** to open the full Quick Settings panel
2. Find the **Airplane Mode** tile (it will be highlighted/active)
3. Tap it so it's no longer highlighted
   - *Shortcut:* Open **Settings → Network & internet**, then toggle **Airplane mode** off

After you turn it off, wait about 30–60 seconds to let your phone re-register on the network. Then check your status bar again — you should see your signal bars return along with a network type like 5G or LTE.

**Once you've done that, please try:**
- Making a test phone call
- Loading a webpage using mobile data (make sure you're off Wi-Fi)

Let me know what you see in the status bar afterward and whether calls and data are working now. If service still doesn't come back, I'll keep troubleshooting with you — there are a few other things we can check.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, I've turned Airplane Mode off. Let me check the status bar again.

turns.thought:
I understand the frustration — let's keep digging. The good news is the airplane icon is gone, so that step worked. There are a couple of other things that commonly cause this.

Let me first check your device record on our side:

No worries — that was still a good step, and it's actually useful information! Two things stand out in what you're seeing now:

1. **"No Signal"** — your phone still isn't connecting to the network at all
2. **"Data Disabled"** — your mobile data switch is also turned off

Let's tackle the easy one first, then dig into the signal problem.

**Step 1 — Turn mobile data back ON**

Since Airplane Mode was on, it's possible that got flipped too:

- **iPhone:** Settings → Cellular (or Mobile Data) → toggle **Cellular Data** to green/on
- **Android:** Settings → Network & internet → SIMs (or Mobile network) → toggle **Mobile data** on
  - *Quick way:* Swipe down twice from the top to open Quick Settings and tap the **Mobile data** tile

**Step 2 — Check your SIM card**

This is my main suspect for the "No Signal" part, since our system shows your device had an eSIM transfer on January 20 and a more recent activation on February 15. Go to:

- **iPhone:** Settings → General → About → look for the SIM/eSIM entry
- **Android:** Settings → About phone → SIM status

Or just run the **check_sim_status** diagnostic on your device if you have it handy and tell me what it reports. You're looking for "Active." If it reports **Missing**, please do a **reseat_sim_card** — power the phone off, remove and reinsert the SIM (or re-download the eSIM profile), then power it back on.

**Step 3 — Check your APN settings**

Incorrect APN settings are another common cause of no-service-after-a-fix. Run **check_apn_settings** on your device. If it reports anything other than correct/default, do a **reset_apn_settings**, then **reboot_device** — the reboot is required for the change to take effect.

Try Step 1 and 2 first and let me know:
- Does the signal bar come back at all after enabling data?
- What does the SIM status say?
- What does the APN check report?

From there I'll know whether we need to move on to a network mode check or get a specialist involved. You're doing great so far — these steps usually shake it loose.

**One quick note first:** the fact that it *still* says "Data Disabled" even after you turned mobile data on is normal-ish here — when a phone has no cellular connection at all, it often keeps showing data as disabled regardless of the switch. So I wouldn't read too much into that yet. The real thing to fix is **"No Signal."** Data should come back on its own once we restore the connection.

**Next step — let's check your SIM card.**

That's actually a very useful finding — and it's very likely your root cause. A SIM card the phone can't detect means the phone has nothing to identify itself to the network with, which produces exactly what you're seeing: no signal, no data, even with Airplane Mode off.

**Let's reseat the SIM — this is usually all it takes.**

Since your device is an eSIM-capable **Smartphone Pro Max**, the steps differ slightly depending on whether you're using a physical SIM or an eSIM:

**If you have a physical SIM card:**
1. **Power the phone completely off** — don't just lock the screen
2. Locate the SIM tray (usually a small pinhole on the side or bottom edge)
3. Insert the **SIM eject tool** (or a straightened paperclip) into the hole and press firmly until the tray pops out
4. Pull the tray out and **remove the SIM card**
5. Check the gold contacts on the SIM — if they look dirty, gently wipe them with a clean, dry, lint-free cloth. Also check for any cracks or damage
6. **Reinsert the SIM** into the tray, making sure it sits flat and is oriented correctly (the notched corner lines up with the tray's notch)
7. Push the tray firmly back in until it's flush with the phone body
8. **Power the phone back on**
9. Wait about 1–2 minutes for it to re-register on the network

**If you're on an eSIM (no physical card):**

The equivalent fix would be re-downloading your eSIM profile, but **I'm not able to push that to your line myself** — that would require our technical support team. Let me know if that's your setup and I'll get you handed off.

**After you power back on:**
- Run **check_sim_status** again — we want it to say "Active"
- Check the status bar for signal bars
- Try a test call

Go ahead and try the reseat, then let me know what the SIM status reports afterward. If it now says "Active" but you *still* have no bars, we'll move on to checking your APN settings — that's the next most likely culprit. And if the SIM is physically damaged, or it still isn't detected after reseating, we'll need to get a replacement card or eSIM issued, which I can arrange through a specialist.
